History of Present Illness:
48-year-old man. Twenty-four hours of persistent right upper abdominal pain after several shorter episodes over the past month. Appetite is poor.

Physical Examination:
Right subcostal tenderness with inspiratory arrest; no diffuse guarding. Temperature 37.7 C; heart rate 112/min; BP 122/70 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 16.2 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.1 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 283 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 136 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 126 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 41 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 66 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 52 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 103 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: gallbladder-neck stone, 5 mm wall thickening and increased mural vascularity; common bile duct 4 mm.
